analysis.medium: charcoal and white chalk on gray paper
analysis.subject: human skull, three-quarter view, lit from upper left
analysis.summary: A skull turned three-quarters left, lit from the upper left so the right side falls into a deep cast shadow. The big forms are the cranium dome and the jaw; the eye sockets and nose are the darkest accents.
uncertainties: Exact tooth count is hard to see

learning_goal: Build a skull from its big forms, then model it with a few tonal steps
buddy_intro: Let’s build the skull from two big forms first, then carve the sockets and shade.

steps.title: Place the cranium and jaw
steps.instruction: Lightly draw the cranium dome (shape 1) and the lower jaw (shape 2) as two big ovals.
steps.why: Two big forms fix the size and angle before any detail.
steps.tip: Use the side of the charcoal stick, very light pressure.

steps.title: Mark the eye sockets and nose
steps.instruction: Mark the two eye sockets (shapes 1–2) and the nasal opening (shape 3) as simple dark shapes.
steps.why: The sockets and nose set the face’s proportions; everything else hangs off them.
steps.tip: Keep them slightly smaller than you think — you can widen them later.

steps.title: Block in the cast shadow
steps.instruction: Fill shape 1 with your darkest tone, pressing firmly, and give shape 2 a medium tone.
steps.why: The darkest shapes set the contrast every other tone is judged against.
steps.tip: Squint — the shadow joins into one shape.

steps.title: Lift out the lights
steps.instruction: Pull light out of the forehead (shape 1) and cheekbone (shape 2) with the eraser.
steps.why: Lights read brightest next to deep darks.
steps.tip: Press a kneaded eraser, do not rub.

tips.title: Squint
tips.body: Squint to merge details into big shapes.
